subject: science
passage: Meerkats, small mongooses of southern Africa, forage in groups, and at almost any moment one member stands upright on a mound or bush, scanning for hawks and jackals while the others dig for insects. This sentinel behavior was long described as a sacrifice: the guard, it was assumed, gave up feeding time to protect its companions. Yet when researchers tracked individual meerkats in the Kalahari Desert, they found that animals most often took up guard duty soon after they had eaten well, and that a sentinel given extra food guarded for longer. Standing watch, it seems, is what a meerkat does when it has little left to gain from foraging.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To describe the dangers that hawks and jackals pose to foraging meerkats
choices.B: To challenge an explanation of meerkat sentinel behavior by presenting evidence about when meerkats stand guard
choices.C: To explain how researchers tracked individual meerkats in the Kalahari Desert
choices.D: To argue that sentinel behavior provides no real protection to a meerkat group

explanation.why: The text first gives the old explanation of sentinel behavior (a "sacrifice" of feeding time) and then, with "Yet," reports what researchers found: meerkats stand guard mainly when they are already well fed. The final sentence draws the new conclusion. The purpose is to challenge the old explanation using that evidence.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Predators are mentioned only in the first sentence to explain what the sentinel watches for; they are not the focus of the text.
explanation.B: Correct. The text sets up the "sacrifice" explanation, then uses the Kalahari findings about well-fed meerkats to replace it with a different account.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text mentions that researchers tracked meerkats but says nothing about how they did it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text questions why a meerkat stands guard, not whether guarding protects the group. It never says the behavior is useless.
